rule: good. context only and never parsed; texts 1 and 2 carry the storing half and text 4 the feeding half, each needing the small edit below.
texts: mixed: the rule fires and the storing is covered, but 'the Keepers' — a capitalized plural — is read as a proper name rather than as a plural of 'keeper', so the parse had to invent a group of keepers that the naming rule does not allow, and nothing ties these Keepers to the 'keeper' kind your other rules range over. Lower-case the plural so it stays the same kind word your singular sentences use: 'When mire-essence forms in the cauldron, the keepers store the mire-essence in clay vessels.'

mixed: same single problem as text 1 — the capitalized plural 'the Keepers' is read as a proper name, so the parse invented an unlicensed group of keepers and left them unconnected to the 'keeper' kind; everything else about the rule is right and it fires. Lower-case the plural: 'Whenever mire-essence forms in the cauldron, the keepers keep the mire-essence in clay vessels.'

bad: 'stored mire-essence' puts a state word in front of a bare mass noun with no article, so there is nothing for 'stored' to be true of — the parse welded the two into a single kind, 'stored-mire-essence', which the instruction set bars for a descriptive state word, and the sentence's own text 4 splits the same phrase the other way, so the two records do not match. Give the essence an article so the drawn portion can carry both the kind and the state: 'Each Keeper draws some stored mire-essence when that Keeper tends a lantern.'

mixed: the rule is right and fires, but the 'will' is dropped, so a future claim is recorded as a timeless habit — and the instruction set does not settle whether a 'will' claim about a bare kind is a general rule at all. If you mean the standing rule the surrounding sentences state, use the plain present: 'Stored mire-essence feeds lantern lighting.'
